properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 by comparing the design's CONSUMES edges against what the code actually imports. THREE OF THE FIVE `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces are consumed, in the graph, by a component that does not use them in the build.

  interface                     design says CONSUMED BY   code actually imports it in
  ifc:req-dyno-graph-api        cmp:propagate             structure.rs, allocate.rs, flow.rs  (cmp:structure / cmp:allocate / cmp:flow)
  ifc:req-dyno-vector-api       cmp:search                dimensions.rs                       (cmp:dimensions)
  ifc:req-dyno-resolution-api   cmp:heal                  seam.rs, ingest.rs                  (cmp:seam / cmp:ingest)
  ifc:req-dyno-core-api         cmp:graph                 graph.rs and throughout             CORRECT
  ifc:req-dyno-storage-api      sys:store                 the store                           CORRECT

VERIFIED BOTH WAYS: `propagate.rs` contains no `use dynograph_graph`, `search.rs` no `use dynograph_vector`, `heal.rs` no `use dynograph_resolution`; while `structure.rs`, `dimensions.rs` and `seam.rs` each do. And `art:structure` REALIZES `cmp:structure`, which is a different node from `cmp:propagate`, so this is misattribution rather than a naming synonym.

WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE. A CONSUMES edge is a black-box boundary claim: it says WHICH PART of this system depends on that supplier. Three of five point at the wrong part, so the design's answer to 'what breaks if the graph API changes?' names `cmp:propagate` and misses the three components that would actually break. That matters directly for `dec:a-black-box-needs-three-edges-not-one` and any future SE work on the subsystem tier, because those are the same edges the black-box decomposition will rest on.

PLAUSIBLE CAUSE, not verified: the edges look like they were drawn from what each interface is FOR (propagation is the graph-algorithm-shaped feature, search is the vector-shaped feature, heal is the fuzzy-matching-shaped feature) rather than from what imports what. That is a reasonable-sounding guess written down once and never checked against the build — which is the class of error `reconcile_artifacts` catches for FILES and nothing catches for EDGES.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ REPAIRED 2026-08-19 on Anthony's word ("do both 1 & 2"), and it is a resync of the RECORD, not a fix to the system — the code was right throughout. `chg:foundation-consumes-redrawn-from-imports-2026-08-19`, change_type `resync`, subject `record`.

THE IMPORTS WERE RE-VERIFIED AGAINST CURRENT HEAD before anything was redrawn, rather than trusting this two-day-old measurement, and they were unchanged:
  dynograph_graph      -> allocate.rs, flow.rs, structure.rs
  dynograph_vector     -> dimensions.rs
  dynograph_resolution -> ingest.rs, seam.rs

RETRACTED (3): cmp:propagate -> graph-api, cmp:search -> vector-api, cmp:heal -> resolution-api.
DRAWN (5), each `weight_basis: evidence` because they come from imports rather than from a guess:
  ifc:req-dyno-graph-api      <- cmp:structure, cmp:allocate, cmp:flow
  ifc:req-dyno-vector-api     <- cmp:dimensions  (optional, weight 0.4)
  ifc:req-dyno-resolution-api <- cmp:ingest

Note the shape change: one interface now has THREE consumers where the design claimed one. The old edges were not merely mis-pointed, they were under-counted — 'what breaks if the graph API changes?' had one answer and now has three.

⚠️ DID THE REPAIR REACH THE CAUSE? PARTLY, AND THE HONEST ANSWER IS NO.
· The three wrong edges are corrected — that is the symptom.
· THE CAUSE IS UNADDRESSED: nothing checks a CONSUMES edge against what the build actually imports. `reconcile_artifacts` does exactly this job for FILES and there is no equivalent for EDGES, which is what let a plausible guess sit unchallenged from whenever it was drawn until 2026-08-17. Until something computes it, the next such edge will be as wrong and as unnoticed.

🛑 AND ONE ENDPOINT COULD NOT BE DRAWN, so the repair is incomplete on its own terms. `seam.rs` imports `dynograph_resolution` and there is NO `cmp:seam` — the original measurement named one, and it does not exist. `art:seam` and `art:seam-test` are registered and REALIZE no Component at all. Rather than invent a component to complete a tidy picture, the edge was left undrawn and the gap recorded here: ifc:req-dyno-resolution-api has ONE consumer in the graph and TWO in the build.
